notes:
## Fixes since v1.1.0

- Show only windows belonging to the current Space of each display. Fullscreen windows no longer leave a button behind on their former Desktop; minimized windows and manual ordering remain preserved.
- Hide all taskbars and popups in Mission Control through native AppKit behavior. Preserve fullscreen visibility when focus moves to system UI or a temporary state read fails.
- Restore automatic height adjustment for Chrome windows created from a fullscreen window and later returned to the Desktop. Preserve the window's top edge and menu-bar inset, and recover from changed geometry without leaving stale suppression behind.
- Refresh a window's Space membership immediately when it moves between monitors, removing the previous wait for the periodic refresh.
- Show ordinary windows of standalone menu-bar applications, including Stats Dashboard. Keep observing the application after its last window closes so a reopened window appears promptly.
- Serialize window commands and cancel obsolete external operations, preventing an older minimize or activation from overtaking a newer command.
- Preserve pending window restoration after failed or unverified writes and across temporary Accessibility uncertainty. An unchanged monitor no longer has its windows restored when another display changes.
- Move Accessibility observer setup off the main thread, bound each AX operation, cancel outdated registrations and reject stale callbacks. Transient observation failures recover without an immediate retry loop.
- Stop fast per-window polling once windows have settled; retain event-driven refresh and the existing low-frequency fallback.
- Recover application icons after a temporary lookup failure and refresh existing buttons without requiring a window-list change.
- Release terminated-process state, bound process-identity caches and remove completed cancelled-operation references.
- Handle startup without available displays and display disconnect/reconnect safely.
- Remove obsolete app-only cards, unused UI/model code and inactive compatibility branches.

## Verification

The complete unit suite, constrained Swift-executor checks, tooling checks and Apple Silicon Release build passed. Regression checks reproduce the reviewed defects on the previous code and pass on the corrected code. Automated UI checks run offscreen; no live permission revocation is used.

No new privacy permissions, global input monitoring, screen capture or third-party runtime dependencies are introduced.
